item.title: A market board for Fiber swaps: hubs advertise, wallets discover (1 posts)
item.description: Bitcoin assets have been arriving on CKB for a while now. RGB++ gives them a way in, and Fiber gives them speed once they’re here. But something basic was missing in between: if you hold one of these assets and want to swap it, how do you find out who’ll take it, and at what rate? There was no answer that didn’t involve asking around. So I built the answer: a gossip-native market for Fiber swaps. Hubs broadcast signed, expiring rate offers over the same gossip the network already uses for routing info. Any wallet can list the offers and take the best one. No negotiation, no middleman, no new network to run, three RPC calls (`publish`, `list`, `best-rate`), a CLI group, and a one-file web...

item.title: Khie，「契」。 (1 posts)
item.description: Just tried NervDAO + CCC App Khie + MetaMask, pairing is fast, hints are clear, the whole flow was super smooth. Great work! A peer-to-peer wallet connector is something the crypto industry has needed for a long time. The industry is still stuck in the “centralized frontend + web2 page injection” paradigm that MetaMask established. Khie shows that wallets and apps can simply meet each other across devices and platforms, without either side being locked into the browser or dependent on centralized relays. It’s also an essential abstraction for the local-first and Web5 stack. When apps run on the user’s own devices and don’t depend on any server, they need a way to reach the user’s wallet...

item.title: A Revenue Layer for CKB Nodes (2 posts)
item.description: What if CKB nodes could become a revenue-generating opportunity? The Problem CKB nodes operate at a cost. Unlike Proof-of-Stake chains, they receive no reward stream. The approximately 576 nodes listed on https://nodes.ckb.dev/ are operated by altruists, foundations, and exchanges. This model is fundamentally unsustainable at scale. The Core Idea What if nodes could earn fees by running optional services for applications? No protocol changes required. Applications pay for the services they use. Nodes collect fees for providing them. item.title: Can we pay Nodes similar to POW miners using the Secondary Issuance? (1 posts)
item.description: Great question on incentivizing nodes. I’d like to propose a complementary angle: nodes earning fees by providing services—without touching secondary issuance. Instead of protocol-level rewards, what if nodes made money by running optional services that applications actually pay for? Event-watching, storage, oracles, computation validation—each service independent, each with real economic demand. I’ve posted more details here: A Revenue Layer for CKB Nodes Both approaches could coexist—secondary issuance for baseline support, service fees for revenue-generating operators. Thoughts?
